sources.title: Ken Kirigaya, Tay (Shan) Encroachments into the Irrawaddy Basin and the Fall of Ava, Journal of the Siam Society 106 (2018)
sources.note: PDF pp245 to 248: abstract and opening argument. Conquest of Ava in 1527 and commercial interpretation. Does not establish one state across the imported outline.

sources.title: U Thaw Kaung, Accounts of King Bayinnaung’s Life and Hanthawadi Hsinbyu-myashin Ayedawbon
sources.note: Selected Writings, printed pp35 to 37,42: 1557 multilingual bell; conquests; policy of reinstatement after allegiance. Avoid the chapter’s erroneous 1557 Chiang Mai date and differing exact day conversions.

sources.title: Jingli Bai, Sino-Burmese overland trade under dual-overlordship system in Qing dynasty (2021)
sources.note: Chulalongkorn University thesis abstract: seventeenth to early twentieth centuries, multiple overlordship, caravan/river commodities. Sipsong Panna is a comparative eastern network, not an alias for this map record.

sources.title: Christian Daniels, Strategic fluidity: Expansion by Kengtung (Chiang Tung) into Siam-controlled Lan Na, 1869 to 1892
sources.note: Introduction: Konbaung 1752 to 1885, lowland wet rice and upland swidden; annexation and multiple allegiances. Historical introduction used for regional scope, not later military events projected into 1530.

sources.title: Jana Igunma, Revelations from historical stone inscriptions in Shan State, British Library (24 March 2026)
sources.note: Or16785/C ff1 to 2, front1537 and left side1600; Punjaburi’s partial translations; two rubbings belong to one fragmented stone. 400 rice fields with people/farmers is the curator’s translation, not an independently reconstructed census.

sources.title: Jotika Khur-Yearn, The Poetic Dhamma of Zao Amat Long’s Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta
sources.note: SOAS thesis, printed pp30 to 31: Dhammadinna1541 to 1640, Sutta Nibbāna title/translation, teacher at Wan Khang. Direct PDF fetch failed; indexed original and full-text studyres transcription agree. Biography is traditional; not an autograph date.

sources.title: Myo Thant Linn and Maria Kekki, Collected by a botanist: the Rylands’ only Shan manuscript (2024)
sources.note: Sections What is the Rylands Shan manuscript about?, Suspended book, The botanist who also collected manuscripts. Tai Mao manuscript of Dhammadinna text, no completion year, acquired1932. Do not turn proposed sisters/daughters relationship into fact.

sources.title: Jana Igunma, A bar of pure gold: Shan Buddhist manuscripts (2025 revision of British Library essay)
sources.note: Primary curator account republished by SEACOM. Or12040 dated1885 caption: ဗုဒ္ဓါနူဿတိ, Buddhānūssati; next paragraph translates recollections of the Buddha. Or14572 dated1894 weighs over2kg. Treat original BL version and this revised post as one work.

sources.title: Leslie Milne, Shans at Home (1910), contemporary colonial-era observations
sources.note: Printed p45 Children’s Food, p100 The Home. Direct PDF fetch failed; original scan indexed text reproduced with exact title/phrase queries. Colonial author’s local observations, no claim of unchanged pre1783 practice; racist generalizations and medical claims omitted.

sources.title: Jotika Khur-Yearn, Uncovering Shan Manuscripts at SOAS Library (15 September 2025)
sources.note: Paragraph on scope of manuscript subjects and fig4 tattooing; collection includes dated1901 material. Does not date all medical texts to map centuries or establish efficacy/sanitation.

sources.title: Robbins Burling, Boys of the Yellow Robe, Penn Museum Expedition (1961)
sources.note: Opening Hopong market/compensation of sawbwas; modern observation. Byline directly verified. Five-day market, Pa-oh sellers, garlic and strawberries, continuation after royal power purchased.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact imported1530 to 1783, five contiguous geometry intervals. Only this ID claimed. Scan also found lan-na1600 to 1783, kept separate: distinct record with potentially erroneous Ayutthaya alias requires its own identity review. Ahom, Tai-related empires, modern Myanmar, Kushan and unrelated American names are not aliases. Outline is drastically broad: bbox1530 to 1650=91.55,20.96,98.98,28.41; later=90.00,20.92,100.04,28.41. Public caveat included; no unverified repair. Many later tangible household and writing witnesses clearly labelled after1783. No hypothetical sanitation infrastructure invented.
